newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka '96 petroleum product imports up 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka '96 petroleum product imports up 30 pct.

text.p: Sri Lanka's imports of refined petroleum products rose 30 percent to 729,000 tonnes last year from 562,000 tonnes in 1995, according to provisional figures in the Central Bank's 1996 annual report.
The sharp rise in the imports was because of increased diesel power generation to meet a shortfall in hydropower generation caused by drought, it said.

The Indian Ocean island had to endure power cuts of up to eight hours a day during the height of the drought last year after water levels in hydropower reservoirs, which supply the bulk of electricity, fell to dangerously low levels.

The value of refined petroleum products imported in 1996 rose 76 percent to 8.5 billion rupees ($144 million) from 4.8 billion rupees in 1995, said the Central Bank report released on Wednesday. ($1=Rs 59.18)
